justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across horizons, starting near 89.1 for the one-day forecast, edging to 89.5 at one week, and reaching 90.5 at one month. The one-day estimate is anchored heavily on recent price momentum and mean-reversion tendencies — essentially, I expect the asset to trade close to its current level with a slight positive bias based on short-term trend continuation. As the horizon extends to one week and one month, I incorporated a small structural drift premium, reflecting the general tendency of risk assets to appreciate over time when no major macro disruption is imminent. The gradual upward slope in point estimates is intentional but conservative, acknowledging that near-term catalysts are limited and the current price already reflects most available information.

The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, going from a relatively tight 5.2-point spread at one day to an 11-point spread at one week and a 21-point spread at one month. At the one-day horizon, intraday volatility is fairly predictable and large gaps are uncommon absent a scheduled news event, so I kept the interval narrow. At one week, uncertainty compounds because macroeconomic data releases, central bank communications, and shifts in market sentiment can all materially move prices. By one month, the full range of possible macro scenarios, earnings reports, geopolitical developments, and liquidity conditions widens the distribution considerably, and I chose an interval that reflects roughly 1.5 to 2 standard deviations of typical monthly price variation.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, an unexpected hawkish policy surprise from a major central bank, a sudden deterioration in credit conditions, or a geopolitical shock could easily breach the lower bounds, particularly at the one-week and one-month horizons. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected economic data release or a risk-on sentiment shift driven by easing inflation signals could push prices above 101 over the month. Liquidity events — such as a large forced seller or a short squeeze — represent tail risks that are by definition underweighted in standard volatility-based intervals and could cause rapid moves in either direction that my confidence bands do not fully capture.
